sources_considered.why: Primary description of DeepSeek's rule-based rewards and selection of generated training examples; contextual evidence for one model family.
Primary disclosure of substantial synthetic-data use, but not a population-wide measurement of symbolic-generated data.
Search result concerns a later transparency report and does not provide a representative July 2025 model census.

evidence_items.locator: Section 2.3.3, Rejection Sampling and Supervised Fine-Tuning
evidence_items.explanation: The report describes rule-based rewards, compiler feedback, and approximately 600,000 selected reasoning examples. This establishes symbolic involvement in one training pipeline, but neither a majority of models nor the prevalence of training directly on symbolic-system outputs.

The surrounding sections describe increased synthetic-data use and generation by Qwen models. They do not quantify the share generated by symbolic rule systems; the entire five-trillion-token stage cannot be counted as such data.

unresolved_gaps: No representative census establishes how many contemporary models meet the claim.
The reviewed disclosures do not quantify substantial symbolic-generated data use across the relevant population.
Evidence of synthetic text and rule-based rewards does not independently settle the stronger claim about generation by symbolic systems.
